ENGLISH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17
====

GRADE: Grade 8
SUBJECT: ENGLISH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

2. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. happiness
   C. blue
   D. run

3. When practising : Stressed and unstressed words, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” : Stressed and unstressed words.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to : Stressed and unstressed words.
   D. Copy random text without understanding : Stressed and unstressed words.

4. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. went
   C. going
   D. goes

5. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the Library
   B. Where is the library?
   C. Where is the library
   D. where is the library

6. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. A person, place, thing, or idea
   B. Only an action
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only a joining word

7. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.

8. When practising Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

9. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.

10. When practising Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

11. When practising Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.

12. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. Many unrelated topics with no link
   C. No full stops
   D. Only one word repeated

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Writing process – dialogues 13.5.1 Narrative Composition 14.5.1 Descriptive writ and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Writing 12.5.1 The writing process and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Extensive Listening: Poems and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.4.1 Intensive Reading: Short Stories.

2. D — run

3. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for : Stressed and unstressed words.

4. B — went

5. B — Where is the library?

6. A — A person, place, thing, or idea

7. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Oral Presentations: Songs.

8. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 15.3.1 Types of Sentences: Interrogative sentences.

9. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading: Simple poems.

10. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1Extensive Reading: Independent Reading.

11. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Sounds: vowels /ɑː/ /зː/and consonants /tʃ/ and/dʒ/ 9.1.1.2: Stressed and unstre.

12. A — One main idea with supporting sentences

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading 12.4.1: Short Story: Characters; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing process – dialogues 13.5.1 Narrative Composition 14.5.1 Descriptive writ; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Writing 12.5.1 The writing process; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening and Speaking 13.1.1 Extensive Listening: Poems; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
